title: A1 Capstone Review & Mastery Benchmark
subtitle: Synthesize all A1 grammatical systems and verify readiness for CEFR A2 progression
grammarFocus: Sentence Bracket (Satzklammer with Modals & Separable Verbs)

concept.title: The Unified A1 Grammar Synthesis
concept.explanation:
Congratulations on reaching the capstone unit of Level A1! At this stage, you have acquired all foundational structural pillars of the German language. Before advancing to the Dative case and subordinate clauses of A2, we consolidate all systems into a single mental framework.

### The 5 Architectural Pillars of A1

1. **Gender & Case Identification**:
   - Every German noun has a gender: <nom>der</nom>, <nom>die</nom>, or <nom>das</nom>.
   - The subject is always in the **Nominative** case.
   - The direct object is in the **Accusative** case.
   - Only the **masculine gender** changes in the accusative: *der* → *den*, *ein* → *einen*, *kein* → *keinen*.

2. **Verb Conjugation & Stem Mutations**:
   - Regular personal endings: *-e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en*.
   - The two auxiliary pillars: *haben* and *sein*.
   - Strong verbs mutate their stem vowels (*e → i*, *e → ie*, *a → ä*) exclusively in the 2nd (*du*) and 3rd person singular (*er/sie/es*).

3. **Word Order & The V2 Rule**:
   - In declarative main clauses, the conjugated verb is permanently anchored in **Position 2**.
   - If a time or place expression takes Position 1, the subject steps to Position 3 (**Inversion**).
   - ADUSO conjunctions (*aber, denn, und, sondern, oder*) occupy **Position 0**.

4. **The Sentence Bracket (Die Satzklammer)**:
   - **Modal Verbs**: Conjugated modal at Position 2, infinitive main verb at the very end.
   - **Separable Verbs**: Conjugated verb stem at Position 2, separable prefix at the very end.

5. **Precision in Negation & Questions**:
   - Use *kein-* for nouns with indefinite or zero articles.
   - Use *nicht* for verbs, adjectives, adverbs, and nouns with definite articles.
   - Contradict negative questions with the affirmative particle *doch*!
   - Use *um* for clock time, *am* for days/dates, and *im* for months/seasons.

deepDives.title: A1 to A2 Readiness Milestone
deepDives.content: To be truly ready for A2, you must produce these A1 structures automatically, without pausing to translate from your native language. If you score 80% or higher on the Capstone Evaluation below, you have successfully attained the CEFR A1 Breakthrough standard!

workedExamples.german: Jeden Morgen muss ich um halb sieben aufstehen, aber heute darf ich lange schlafen.
workedExamples.english: Every morning I have to get up at half past six, but today I am allowed to sleep in.

guidedPractice.instruction: Identify the direct object case: fill in the masculine accusative article:
guidedPractice.prompt: Der Student sucht ___ neuen Computer. (der Computer)
guidedPractice.explanation: 'der Computer' is the masculine direct object in accusative: den neuen Computer.

guidedPractice.instruction: Arrange into an inverted declarative sentence with a separable verb:
guidedPractice.explanation: Morgen (Pos 1) + rufe (Verb Pos 2) + ich (Subject Pos 3) + dich (Object) + an (Prefix at end).

guidedPractice.prompt: Haben Sie ein Auto? — Nein, ich habe ___ Auto.
guidedPractice.explanation: 'das Auto' is neuter. The negative article for an indefinite neuter noun is 'kein'.

guidedPractice.instruction: Transform into an imperative addressed to 'du':
guidedPractice.prompt: Transform 'Du sprichst leise' into a command:
guidedPractice.explanation: Drop 'du' and '-st', keeping the e → i shift: 'Sprich leise!'

guidedPractice.prompt: Der Zug kommt ___ 14:15 Uhr ___ Gleis 3 an.
guidedPractice.explanation: Clock time is always introduced with 'um': um 14:15 Uhr.

readingPassage.title: Mein erstes Jahr in Deutschland (My First Year in Germany)
readingPassage.germanText: Vor einem Jahr bin ich nach Berlin gekommen. Am Anfang war alles neu und nicht einfach: Ich konnte kaum Deutsch sprechen und verstand die Schilder am Bahnhof nicht. Aber ich habe jeden Tag gelernt. Jeden Morgen bin ich früh aufgestanden, habe die Zeitung gelesen und viele Vokabeln wiederholt. Heute habe ich viele deutsche Freunde, arbeite in einem Architekturbüro und kann mich ohne Probleme verständigen. Nun freue ich mich auf die nächsten Schritte!
readingPassage.englishSummary: A year ago I arrived in Berlin. In the beginning everything was new and not easy: I could hardly speak German and didn't understand the signs at the train station. But I studied every day. Every morning I got up early, read the newspaper, and reviewed many vocabulary words. Today I have many German friends, work at an architecture office, and can communicate without problems. Now I am looking forward to the next steps!

comprehensionQuestions.question: What difficulty did the author face in the beginning?
options: He could hardly speak German and didn't understand the signs
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: The text states: 'Ich konnte kaum Deutsch sprechen und verstand die Schilder am Bahnhof nicht.'

comprehensionQuestions.question: What is the author's situation today?
options: He works in an architecture office and communicates without problems
He is still looking for work
comprehensionQuestions.explanation: The text states: '...arbeite in einem Architekturbüro und kann mich ohne Probleme verständigen.'

listeningDialogue.title: Erfolg bei der Zertifikatsprüfung (Success in the Exam)

lines.speaker: Prüfer
lines.text: Herzlichen Glückwunsch, Frau Rossi! Sie haben die A1-Prüfung mit 92 Punkten bestanden.
lines.translation: Congratulations, Mrs. Rossi! You passed the A1 exam with 92 points.

lines.speaker: Kandidatin
lines.text: Vielen Dank! Das freut mich riesig. War mein Sprechteil gut?
lines.translation: Thank you very much! That makes me very happy. Was my speaking portion good?

lines.speaker: Prüfer
lines.text: Ausgezeichnet! Ihre Satzstruktur und Ihre Verbendungen waren fast fehlerfrei. Wann möchten Sie mit A2 weitermachen?
lines.translation: Excellent! Your sentence structure and verb endings were almost error-free. When would you like to continue with A2?

lines.speaker: Kandidatin
lines.text: Direkt nächsten Monat! Mein Ziel ist das Goethe-Zertifikat B2.
lines.translation: Directly next month! My goal is the Goethe-Zertifikat B2.

questions.question: What score did Frau Rossi achieve on her A1 examination?
questions.explanation: The examiner explicitly states: '...mit 92 Punkten bestanden.'

writing.prompt: Write a comprehensive A1 capstone profile of yourself (5 to 8 sentences). Combine greetings, where you come from and live, your profession/studies, your daily routine with times and separable verbs, what you must or want to do, and your goal for learning German.
guidelines: Include at least one sentence with V2 inversion (e.g. 'Morgens stehe ich um...')
Include at least one sentence with an accusative direct object (e.g. 'Ich kaufe einen...')
Include at least one modal verb with Satzklammer (e.g. 'Ich will fließend Deutsch sprechen')
Include correct temporal prepositions (um, am, im)
writing.sampleResponse: Guten Tag! Mein Name ist Julian und ich komme aus Madrid. Jetzt wohne ich in Berlin und lerne fleißig Deutsch. Jeden Morgen stehe ich um sieben Uhr auf und trinke einen starken Kaffee. Am Vormittag arbeite ich als Grafikdesigner. Ich muss jeden Tag viele E-Mails auf Deutsch schreiben. Am Wochenende treffe ich meine Freunde im Park oder besuche ein Museum. Mein großes Ziel ist das B2-Niveau!
selfCheckRubric: Did you place the conjugated verb in Position 2 in all declarative sentences?
Did you use the accusative shift for masculine nouns (einen starken Kaffee)?
Are all German nouns capitalized throughout?
Did you correctly use the Satzklammer for modal and separable verbs?

speaking.prompt: Demonstrate complete A1 spoken mastery by speaking this capstone sentence aloud:
speaking.targetSentence: Ich lerne seit drei Monaten Deutsch und kann jetzt einfache Gespräche führen.
speaking.translation: I have been learning German for three months and can now hold simple conversations.
speaking.phoneticTips: Pronounce 'Gespräche' with an open rounded 'ä' sound (/ɡəˈʃpʁɛːçə/) and 'führen' with a pure umlaut 'ü' (/ˈfyːʁən/).

questions.instruction: Test 1: Supply the accusative article for 'Schlüssel' (der Schlüssel):
questions.prompt: Ich habe ___ Schlüssel in der Tasche. (der)
questions.explanation: 'der Schlüssel' is masculine direct object in accusative: den Schlüssel.

questions.instruction: Test 2: Where does the main infinitive go in a modal verb sentence?
questions.prompt: In the sentence 'Wir müssen heute die Hausaufgaben ___', where does 'machen' go?
questions.target: machen (at the very end of the sentence)
options: machen (at the very end of the sentence)
questions.explanation: The Satzklammer demands that the infinitive 'machen' stands at the very end.

questions.instruction: Test 3: Invert the word order starting with 'Heute':
questions.explanation: V2 rule: Position 1 is 'Heute', Position 2 MUST be the verb 'fahren', followed by subject 'wir'.

questions.instruction: Test 4: Negating nouns without an article:
questions.prompt: Hast du Zeit? — Nein, ich habe ___ Zeit.
questions.explanation: 'die Zeit' is feminine used with zero-article, requiring 'keine'.

questions.instruction: Test 5: Assemble the separable verb question:
questions.prompt: When do you get up tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Wann (Pos 1) + stehst (Verb Pos 2) + du (Subject Pos 3) + morgen + auf (Prefix at end).

questions.instruction: Test 6: Form the imperative for 'du' from 'sprechen':
questions.explanation: The 'du' command retains the e → i vowel shift: 'Sprich!'
